questions.text: In the Moravel marsh food chain, which organism is the producer?
questions.explanation: Marsh grass is the producer. It makes its own food and is the base of the food chain.

questions.text: Which organism is the primary consumer in the Moravel marsh?
questions.explanation: Marsh hoppers eat the marsh grass directly, so they are the primary consumers.

questions.text: What is the role of glow fungus in the Moravel marsh?
options: It is a producer that makes food from sunlight
It is the top predator that eats silver herons
It is a decomposer that breaks down dead plants and animals and returns nutrients to the soil
It is a primary consumer that eats marsh grass
questions.correctAnswer: It is a decomposer that breaks down dead plants and animals and returns nutrients to the soil
questions.explanation: Glow fungus is the decomposer. It recycles nutrients from dead organisms back into the soil.

questions.text: True or false: If the reed frogs disappeared, the number of marsh hoppers would likely decrease because they would have more predators.
questions.explanation: Reed frogs eat marsh hoppers. Without them, fewer hoppers would be eaten, so the hopper population would rise.

questions.text: Predict what would happen to the marsh hoppers, the marsh grass and the silver herons if the reed frogs disappeared from the Moravel marsh. Explain your reasoning using the food chain.
questions.explanation: Tests understanding of how removing one organism affects others in the food chain.
questions.modelAnswer: Marsh hoppers would increase because the reed frogs, which eat them, are gone. More hoppers would eat more marsh grass, so the grass would decrease. Silver herons eat reed frogs, so they would lose their food source and would likely decrease in number or have to find other food.

criteria.title: Prediction of effects on hoppers and grass

levels.label: Full
levels.description: States that hoppers increase and grass is eaten more/decreases, with a correct link to the loss of frogs.

levels.label: Partial
levels.description: Correctly predicts only one of the effects, or gives the prediction without a clear link.

criteria.title: Effect on silver herons and use of food chain reasoning

levels.label: Full
levels.description: Explains that herons lose their food source and likely decline, using the feeding relationships.

levels.label: Partial
levels.description: Mentions herons being affected but with weak or incomplete reasoning.

levels.label: None
levels.description: Does not address herons or reasoning is incorrect.
